The setup is complete and verified. Here's a summary of what was done:

## Environment setup
- Installed `python3` (3.10.12) and `supervisor` (4.2.1) globally via `apt-get`, non-interactively.
- Fixed `/usr/sbin/policy-rc.d` (was `exit 101`, blocking service starts) and patched `/etc/init.d/supervisor`'s `restart` case, which in the Ubuntu package only stops the daemon without starting it again. Now `service supervisor start|stop|restart|status` all work.

## Supervisord configuration
Created `/etc/supervisor/conf.d/master-worker.conf` with two managed programs:

| Program | Command | Behavior |
|---------|---------|----------|
| `master` | `/usr/bin/python3 /opt/master-worker/master.py` | Writes `job_N.txt` into `/queue` every 10s |
| `worker` | `/usr/bin/python3 /opt/master-worker/worker.py` | Moves files from `/queue` → `/processed`, appends to `/var/log/processed.log` |

Both have `autostart=true` and `autorestart=true` (restart on failure), run under the daemonized supervisord, and log to `/var/log/{master,worker}.log`.

## Verification
- `supervisorctl status` → both `RUNNING` under the supervisord PID.
- Killing `master` with `SIGKILL` triggered an automatic respawn (new PID, `RUNNING`).
- Jobs flow through the pipeline: `/processed/` contains `job_0.txt` … `job_3.txt`, and `/var/log/processed.log` contains matching `Processed job_N.txt` lines.
- A full `service supervisor restart` brings both processes back up cleanly.

The provided `master.py`/`worker.py` scripts were left unmodified (copied to `/opt/master-worker/` for a stable path).
